lesson.title: Distance on a grid

lead.text: A point (x, y) says how far across and how far up it is. The horizontal gap between two points is the difference of their x coordinates.
The vertical gap is the difference of their y coordinates. If a coordinate is negative, count across zero: from −2 to 3 is 5 units.

steps.headline: The gap between two points is the difference of their coordinates.

lead.text: Use the y coordinates this time, which tell you how far up each point is.

reveal.text: You subtracted the y coordinates. The same move works across a grid in either direction.

steps.headline: Find the straight-line distance from (1, 1) to (9, 16).

workedSteps.text: They are the legs of a right triangle. Square and add.

steps.headline: Find the straight-line distance from A (1, 2) to B (4, 6).

lead.text: Find how far apart the points are in each direction first.

reveal.text: The same four moves as before: differences, squares, sum, root.

lead.text: Both ends of a segment are moved: 2 units right and 1 unit up. Ask what happens to the gaps between them.

lesson.orientation: Use coordinate differences as right-triangle legs and distinguish direct distance from a grid path.
lesson.nextAction: Try the next idea, then return for a fresh problem after a delay.

blocks.text: A drone on a grid flies from A (1, 2) to B (4, 6). It goes east first, then north.

intro.promise: By the end you'll find how far apart two points are in a straight line, from their coordinates.

recap.keyIdea: Subtract coordinates to get the horizontal and vertical gaps, then use them as the legs of a right triangle.

blocks.text: You found that the drone's bent route is 7 units, and the straight line from A to B is 5.
You also found 17 units from (1, 1) to (9, 16), and 25 from (0, 1) to (7, 25).

recap.nextHook: Flat shapes have areas. Next, fill a box and count the space inside it.

questions.prompt: A is at (1, 2) and B is at (4, 6). How many units apart are they horizontally?
hints: Horizontal position is the first coordinate.
Subtract the two x coordinates.
Find the absolute value of 4 − 1.
questions.onCorrect: 3. The horizontal gap is the difference of the x coordinates: 4 − 1.

misconceptions.feedback: 5 is the sum of the x coordinates. Subtract them to find the gap.
4 is B's x coordinate. The distance is the gap between the two.

questions.prompt: How many units apart are A (1, 2) and B (4, 6) vertically?
hints: Vertical position is the second coordinate.
Subtract the two y coordinates.
Find the absolute value of 6 − 2.
questions.onCorrect: 4. The vertical gap is the difference of the y coordinates: 6 − 2.

misconceptions.feedback: That adds the y coordinates. Subtract to find the gap.
6 is B's y coordinate. The distance is the gap between the two.

questions.prompt: Find the straight-line distance from A(1, 2) to B(4, 6), in grid units.
hints: Use the horizontal and vertical differences as legs.
Add the squares of the differences.
Calculate √((4 − 1)² + (6 − 2)²).
questions.onCorrect: 5 units. The differences 3 and 4 are legs, so the distance is the square root of 9 + 16.

misconceptions.feedback: 7 is the bent path, 3 across and 4 up. The straight line is shorter.
25 is the square of the distance. Take the square root.

questions.prompt: Both endpoints of a segment move 2 units right and 1 unit up. What happens to its length?
hints: What happens to the gap between the two ends?

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: The same translation leaves both coordinate differences unchanged, so the length is unchanged.

questions.onCorrect: The length stays the same. Both ends move together, so the gaps between them do not change.

misconceptions.feedback: Moving both ends the same way doesn't stretch the segment. The gap between them stays the same.
Nothing is stretched. Both ends move together.

questions.prompt: Find the straight-line distance from (−3, 1) to (5, 7), in grid units.
hints: Subtract corresponding coordinates.
The x difference crosses from negative to positive.
questions.onCorrect: 10 units. Differences 8 and 6, then the square root of 64 + 36.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the bent path, 8 across and 6 up. The straight line is shorter.
100 is the square of the distance. Take the square root.

questions.prompt: Find the straight-line distance from (−3, −4) to (2, 8), in grid units.
hints: Use coordinate differences, not their sum.
Square the horizontal and vertical separations.
questions.onCorrect: 13 units. Differences 5 and 12, then the square root of 25 + 144.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the bent path, across then up. The straight line is shorter.
169 is the square of the distance. Take the square root.

questions.prompt: How many grid units does the drone fly?
hints: How far east does it go?
How far north does it go?
Add the two parts of the journey.
questions.onCorrect: 7. The drone flies 3 units east and 4 units north, and the two parts add.

misconceptions.feedback: That adds all four coordinates. Only the distance flown counts, not the positions.
That is the straight line between the two points, which the drone doesn't fly.

questions.prompt: Why are the two differences the legs of a right triangle?
hints: What angle do a horizontal and a vertical line make?

acceptedIdeas: Going across then up makes a right angle, and the direct line closes the triangle.
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Going across then up makes a right angle, and the direct line closes the triangle.

choices.label: Going across then up makes a right angle, and the direct line closes the triangle.
Because the differences are always equal.
Because the direct line is horizontal.

questions.onCorrect: Across then up meet at a right angle. The straight line between the points is the hypotenuse.

misconceptions.feedback: They can be any two numbers. The right angle comes from going across and then up.
The direct line is slanted. It is the hypotenuse of the triangle.

questions.prompt: Find the straight-line distance from (0, 1) to (7, 25), in grid units.
hints: Find the horizontal and vertical differences.
Square both and add them.
Take the square root of the sum.
questions.onCorrect: 25 units. The differences are 7 and 24, and 49 + 576 = 625.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the bent path, across then up. The straight line is shorter.
625 is the square of the distance. Take the square root.

questions.prompt: Two points are 12 units apart horizontally and 16 units apart vertically. How far apart are they in a straight line?
hints: The two separations are the legs of a right triangle.
Square both and add.
Take the square root of the sum.
questions.onCorrect: 20 units. The legs are 12 and 16, and 144 + 256 = 400.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the bent path, across then up. The straight line is shorter.
400 is the square of the distance. Take the square root.
